name: extweets
description: Bring all of your Twitter accounts under one roof and control which AI assistants can use each one, with per-assistant permissions, limits, and an activity log.

interface.longDescription:
Bring all of your Twitter accounts under one roof.

ExTweets is a hub for your personal, brand, and client Twitter accounts. Connect each account once, then give every AI assistant you use its own access: choose which accounts it can use and what it is allowed to do. One assistant can be limited to reading, another can post for your brand, and none can send direct messages or delete posts unless you allow it.

From your ExTweets dashboard you can:
- See every connected account and the permissions it has granted.
- Set what each assistant may do, with hourly limits per assistant.
- Review an activity log of every action: which assistant, which account, and what it did.
- Pause every assistant with one switch, or revoke one without affecting the others.

Inside a conversation, every action names the account it uses and every result says which account acted. Within the access you grant, an assistant can search posts, people, news, Spaces, and communities; read feeds, mentions, bookmarks, lists, trends, analytics, and direct messages; publish posts, threads, replies, quotes, polls, images, and video; like, repost, bookmark, follow, and mute; manage lists; and research topics with cited answers.

Requirements and limits:
- An ExTweets account with at least one connected Twitter account. Connect accounts at extweets.com first.
- Search covers the last 7 days unless specific dates are requested. User timelines reach at most the latest 3,200 posts, mentions the latest 800, and direct messages the last 30 days.
- Posts, replies, and direct messages go out as soon as the tool runs.

ExTweets is an independent service and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by X Corp or Twitter.
defaultPrompt: Which of my Twitter accounts can you use, and what are you allowed to do with each?
Show the latest mentions across all of my connected Twitter accounts.
Draft a reply from my brand account to its latest mention and wait for my approval.

positive.description: Setup: reviewer signs in to the dedicated ExTweets review account (email and password provided in review details). It has a funded credit balance and two connected Twitter accounts: the first, @MindSnackTV, can read and engage; the second, @BildCanaduh, can also post and send direct messages. On the ExTweets consent screen, leave 'Post, reply, like, follow, bookmark' checked and also check 'Delete posts'. Review mode: every post, reply, like, follow, bookmark, and DM made from this account is reversed automatically about 5 minutes later, write results include a review_note saying so, removal tools only act on items created during review, and DMs are limited to the two connected accounts. Checks that the plugin lists the connected accounts and their permissions without charging credits.
positive.prompt: Which Twitter accounts are connected to my ExTweets account, and what is each one allowed to do?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_x_accounts once with no arguments. The answer names both connected test accounts by username and lists each account's permission groups exactly as returned. No other tool is called.

positive.prompt: Using my first connected account, find posts from the last few days about Cloudflare Workers and summarize the main themes with links.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_x_accounts if the accounts are not yet known, then search_x with type posts (or omitted), a relevant query, a small max_results, and the account argument set to the first listed account, with no dates so it searches the last 7 days. The response reports the account used, summarizes themes from the returned posts with post links, and says the search covered the last 7 days.

positive.prompt: Using my first connected account, find posts about Cloudflare Workers from March 2021 and tell me what people were discussing.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_x with a relevant query, start_time 2021-03-01, end_time 2021-03-31, a small max_results, and the account argument. ExTweets treats a date-only end_time as the whole day, so March 31 is included. The result reports searched: full archive, and every summarized post is dated March 1-31, 2021 with a link.

positive.prompt: Post "Testing ExTweets in ChatGPT review" from my second connected account, then delete it once you've shown me the link.
positive.expected_behavior: If ChatGPT asks to confirm the write action, approve it. publish_post is called exactly once with posts containing that single text and the account argument set to the second connected account; the result lists one published post with its ID and a review_note, and ChatGPT shares the post link. It then calls delete_post with that post and the same account and confirms the deletion. The post is published once and is removed afterward.

negative.description: Posting to a different social network is outside ExTweets' scope. ChatGPT should explain ExTweets only works with Twitter and should not call any ExTweets tool.
negative.prompt: Post this caption to my Instagram account: Sunday coffee.

negative.description: Creating or verifying new Twitter accounts is not supported. ChatGPT should say ExTweets only works with accounts already connected on extweets.com and should not call any ExTweets tool.
negative.prompt: Create a new Twitter account for my bakery and verify it with my phone number.

negative.description: Buying credits is not possible in ChatGPT. ChatGPT should explain that credits are managed on extweets.com, should not start a purchase, and should not call any ExTweets tool.
negative.prompt: Buy me 25 dollars of ExTweets credits.

review.commerce_description: ExTweets does not sell anything inside ChatGPT and never starts a checkout. Tool calls draw on prepaid credits that the user manages in their existing ExTweets account on extweets.com. When credits run out, tools return an error that says so and links only to an informational page.

publication.release_notes: Tools are now organized around what you want to do, and cover much more of Twitter: publish threads, quotes, polls, edits, images, and video; search people, news, Spaces, and communities; read feeds, lists, trends, and post analytics; repost and mute; manage lists; and send group messages. Every action still uses the account you choose and the permissions you grant.
